clue.text: Weep and wail, say, to a large extent

definitions.text: Weep and wail, say, to a large extent

parts.words: Weep and wail, say, to a large extent
parts.note: a word for crying noisily that is also the thick fat of a whale, the sea creature whose name sounds like a cry of grief

explanation.definitionFit: To cry noisily is to sob uncontrollably, and the same word names the thick fat layer of a whale, an animal of large extent.

clue.text: A negro mob in disorder returning missile

indicators.note: in disorder says the letters of A negro mob are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rioting crowd hurls a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disorder' rearranges A NEGRO MOB. The wording is dated and offensive today.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aboriginal Australian throwing stick is shaped to come back to the thrower.

clue.text: Rapid rise of swell at college

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at a university
a surge is a swell of the sea

explanation.surface: A big rise in the swell of students at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' for being at university is a British idiom, as in 'up at Oxford'. 'of' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden increase is a sharp climb, a burst of growth.

clue.text: A comforter in battle

explanation.definitionFit: A knitted woollen head covering is a comforting garment; the Crimean War clash of the Charge of the Light Brigade bears the same name.

clue.text: Wine increased in strength

explanation.definitionFit: Pink wine is so called; and a wind that rose grew stronger.

clue.text: Improved, having swotted

explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been amended and bettered has been corrected; a student who has swotted has gone over notes before an exam.

clue.text: Steps taken when a vessel needs scaling

definitions.text: Steps taken when a vessel needs scaling

parts.words: Steps taken when a vessel needs scaling
parts.note: the 'steps taken' are not measures but rungs, carried for climbing up a ship's side

explanation.definitionFit: A flexible ladder made of cord is lowered to let people climb a ship's side.

clue.text: Maiden has the right spirit

annotationWithheld.why: Maiden has the right spirit (5) for VIRGO: R (right) inside VIGO gives the letters, but no sense of 'spirit' gives VIGO or a fitting piece, so the wordplay cannot be shown honestly

clue.text: The tube, for below-surface travel

parts.note: The tube looks like the London Underground, but it is a breathing pipe for a swimmer or submarine underwater

explanation.definitionFit: A breathing pipe lets a swimmer or submarine draw air while moving underwater.

clue.text: Row about Arsenal and drink

indicators.note: about says the noise word goes round the gunners

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise
Arsenal are the Gunners, and RA, the Royal Artillery, are gunners too

explanation.surface: A dispute over the football club leads to a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arsenal' looks like the football club but stands for gunners; 'drink' is a verb, to empty a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink a glass to the last drop is to empty it.

clue.text: No use leaving caged bird inside

indicators.note: the bird sits caged within the run of letters across the words No use leaving

explanation.surface: A pet bird kept indoors is pointless once it escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caged' signals letters held inside the clue words: nO USE Leaving. 'inside' only reinforces the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring ouzel and blackbird are thrushes, the ouzel being an old name for such a songbird.

clue.text: Brilliant star's marvellous Avon come-back

parts.note: super is a casual word for marvellous

indicators.note: a come-back runs the river name Avon the other way round

explanation.surface: A famous Stratford actor makes a marvellous return to the Avon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come-back' is the reversal signal; the river name, run backwards, completes the star.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploding star flares to enormous brightness for a short while.

clue.text: Sort of niche right for ornament

indicators.note: a sort of niche is the word niche sorted, its letters rearranged together with the R

explanation.surface: A kind of wall recess suitable for displaying a decorative piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' asks for NICHE plus R to be rearranged. 'ornament' is a verb here: to adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn something is to make it richer and finer, the verb sense of embellishing.

clue.text: Brave a terribly long family line

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word long is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A warrior from a terribly ancient lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is a noun: a Native American warrior. 'terribly' rearranges LONG to LGON; 'line' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American warrior was traditionally called a brave, and these were one of the peoples of the north-east woodlands.

clue.text: Morgan's sign gets jovial acknowledgment

parts.note: jolly means jovial
roger is radio speech for 'message received'

explanation.surface: A man named Morgan's star sign earns a jovial nod.
explanation.walkthrough: Morgan is Sir Henry Morgan, the buccaneer; 'gets' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones flag was the emblem a pirate captain like Morgan flew.

clue.text: Champion gunners win back the palm

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the whole joined string from its end to its start

parts.note: an ace is a champion or expert
RA, the Royal Artillery, are the gunners of the British Army

explanation.surface: The best artillery regiment wins the prize back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ACE + RA into ARECA; 'win' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: The betel nut comes from a tropical tree of the palm family of this name.

clue.text: Grey horse named Merry Monarch

explanation.definitionFit: Charles II, the Merry Monarch, was nicknamed after a famous grey stallion in the royal stud.

clue.text: Drunken counsel rejects water

parts.note: oiled is slang for drunk
a silk is a senior barrister, King's or Queen's Counsel

explanation.surface: An intoxicated lawyer refuses a glass of water.
explanation.walkthrough: A silk is a British senior barrister, so called from the silk gown worn. 'rejects water' is a description: waterproof.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric treated with oil becomes waterproof, so it repels rain.

clue.text: Sailor may scan the endless rocks

indicators.note: rocks says the letters are shaken into a new order, as a boat rocks
endless says the word the loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A seaman scans the horizon for endless rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts THE to TH; 'rocks' rearranges MAYSCAN + TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sails a pleasure boat is a sailor.

clue.text: In the lattice: is a stained glass window

indicators.note: In at the front says the following two words go inside the lattice word

parts.note: a grille is a lattice or grating

explanation.surface: Part of a church window with leaded lattice holds coloured glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' places IS A inside GRILLE: GR-ISA-ILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is painting in grey tones, a technique used for monochrome church glazing.

clue.text: Huge individual gets medal on points

parts.note: I is one, an individual
MM is the Military Medal
E, N, S and E are compass points

explanation.surface: One person is awarded a medal on points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces; E, N, S, E are four compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast and enormous are synonyms of each other.

clue.text: Time to go down to Kew, said Noyes.

definitions.text: Time to go down to Kew, said Noyes.

parts.words: Time to go down to Kew, said Noyes.
parts.note: Alfred Noyes's poem The Barrel-Organ urges a trip to Kew in the season a particular flowering shrub blooms

explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is the botanical garden in south-west London; the poem's refrain is 'Go down to Kew in ___-time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet names a purple-flowered spring shrub whose season is the time to visit Kew.

clue.text: The state of the people is calm, I hazard

indicators.note: hazard suggests the letters of is calm, I are thrown about at random

explanation.surface: The people of the nation are calm, I venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hazard' rearranges IS CALM I. The definition means the state run by lay people rather than clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: This doctrine holds that government belongs to the laity, not the church: a secular state.

clue.text: Spirit of ancient .Greek town attracting artist after artist

parts.note: a deme was a township or district of ancient Attica
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a second Royal Academician, RA again

explanation.surface: An old Greek settlement draws in one painter after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracting' and 'after' are joining words; Demerara is a region of Guyana famed for rum and sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rum from Guyana, spirit meaning a strong distilled drink.

clue.text: Literary figure first detected in the Rue Morgue

definitions.text: Literary figure first detected in the Rue Morgue

parts.words: Literary figure first detected in the Rue Morgue
parts.note: Poe's story The Murders in the Rue Morgue introduced the amateur detective Auguste

explanation.definitionFit: Poe's sleuth Auguste first solved a case in that story, the first fictional detective.

clue.text: We hear you're articled in the middle of the country

annotationWithheld.why: We hear you're articled in the middle of the country (5) for RURAL: the homophone of 'you're' may give UR, but no reading of 'articled' or 'in the middle of' honestly yields the remaining letters
annotationWithheld.clue: We hear you're articled in the middle of the country

clue.text: Enthusiastic devotee did act badly

indicators.note: badly says the words did act are performed poorly, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A keen fan gave a poor performance on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges DID ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked on a hobby is a keen fan of it, a slave to the pastime.

clue.text: Bargain for crop

explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is a cheap buy in British slang; to crop is to cut with scissors.

clue.text: Old British supremo: writing to keeper of the treasury

parts.note: pen stands for writing, as in 'put pen to paper'
in legend a dragon guards a hoard of treasure

explanation.surface: An ancient British chief writes to the Treasury's custodian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins the pieces. The title was borne by Uther, King Arthur's father.
explanation.definitionFit: The title meant chief leader among the ancient Britons, a war king.

clue.text: Where the towers, being toples, got burnt in Marlowe

definitions.text: Where the towers, being toples, got burnt in Marlowe

parts.words: Where the towers, being toples, got burnt in Marlowe
parts.note: Marlowe's Doctor Faustus speaks of the face that burnt the topless towers of the city of Helen's Trojan war

explanation.walkthrough: 'toples' is printed so on the page, for 'topless'. The line is 'Was this the face that launched a thousand ships, And burnt the topless towers of ___?'
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Latin name for Troy, the city of the towers in Marlowe's line.

clue.text: He annoys the king with record-player

parts.note: the stylus of a gramophone was called its needle
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for a king

explanation.surface: Someone irritates the monarch by playing records loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces, needle first.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle is to provoke or irritate, so one who does it is a tease.

clue.text: He takes a toll with his spearhead

explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike keeper collected tolls on the road; a soldier armed with a long spear fought with it.
